figures.public_caption: Figure 4. (a) Emission spectra of MoS2 quantum dots (QDs) in solution and when combined with 300 μM folic acid (FA), with an inset showing their visual appearance under 365 nm UV light. (b) Gradual reduction in MoS2 QD emission with increasing FA addition. (c) Emission intensity at 444 nm versus FA concentration, with a Stern−Volmer plot for quenching at lower FA concentrations. (d) Relationship between emission change (ΔI) and FA concentration, with a detailed view of the 0−50 μM range in the inset.

general_background.title: Ligands in solution and at surfaces
general_background.summary: Ligands can associate with dissolved species and particle surfaces, affecting their interactions with the surrounding liquid. A ligand shell compatible with the solvent can provide a barrier to close particle approach, helping a dispersion resist aggregation.
